first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A company that plans weddings in Portugal and gives you one person to deal with. The top is all palaces and cliffs, which looks lovely but a bit grand for us. The bit that kept me was 'a legal wedding in Portugal for foreign couples starts at least one month ahead' and the link 'Check the rules for your passport', because the paperwork is what I'm scared of. Then the guest question straight after has 'Under 30', so I thought, ok, maybe they do small.

attention_map.quote: Many couples hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home.
attention_map.why: Straight away it's talking about the legal side. The palace and cliff headline is pretty but doesn't tell me if it works for 15 people.

attention_map.quote: How many guests? - Under 30 ... What are you celebrating? - Elopement
attention_map.why: First proof that a group our size is on their radar. Elopement is listed as its own thing, not tucked away.

attention_map.quote: Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: One person is nice. Doesn't tell me anything else.

attention_map.quote: Romantic palaces in the Sintra hills that can be booked for a wedding
attention_map.why: Palaces with thrones and scaffolding. Beautiful, but it reads like a big production. I scrolled past on my phone.

I was scanning for guest numbers and it says the same non-answer five times. The airports are useful though, 'Nearest airport: Lisbon (LIS)' is exactly what I want to know. And at least the intro says 'whether you are planning an elopement, a small wedding'.
Not for us. Feels like the big-wedding crowd.

attention_map.quote: A Catholic marriage is legally recognised on its own.
attention_map.why: That answers my church question in one line. 'In the city' with a council space also sounds small and simple.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill ... fees may be charged either way, with a minimum
attention_map.why: So there ARE minimums and they're not telling me what they are. Paying for empty rooms is exactly the worry when you're only bringing close family.

attention_map.section: Plan step by step: Marrying legally tab
attention_map.quote: Witnesses are optional: two to four may take part.
attention_map.why: This is the part I came for. Clear steps, numbered, with government links like Justiça and Smartraveller, and it even explains the CNI for Australians. I actually felt calmer reading it.

attention_map.section: Plan step by step: Costs tab
attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things ... Your Wedded Advisor talks you through the options for your plans.
attention_map.why: No number at all. Not even a starting point. That is the 'wait for the call' thing I hate.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package.
attention_map.why: I came looking for a package for a tiny group and it says there isn't one. The list of welcome dinner, late party, Sunday brunch sounds like a 100-person weekend.

attention_map.section: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.quote: Many quintas have rooms, so your closest guests can stay where you marry
attention_map.why: 'Closest guests' is nice. Rest is about guest websites, not relevant.

attention_map.quote: They walk you through the exact route to marry legally for your nationality
attention_map.why: This is the 'help with everything' I want. It says walk through, not that they do the documents for us, but it's close.

attention_map.quote: Elopements and small weddings are welcome.
attention_map.why: Said out loud, finally. And I can pick 'Under 30', 'Elopement' and 'Catholic', and put budget in the notes. Not too many fields.

attention_map.quote: Can you have a small wedding or elopement in Portugal? Yes. Witnesses are optional ... so two of you can marry with no guests at all
attention_map.why: This is my question word for word. Shame it then says 'for a fee' without saying how much.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity stuff. Nothing to do with us.

questions_answered.question: Does this work for 30 guests or fewer, and is there a smaller package?
questions_answered.evidence: Small groups are welcome ('Elopements and small weddings are welcome', 'Under 30' option, FAQ 'Can you have a small wedding or elopement in Portugal? Yes.'), but 'There is no set Portugal package' and every region card says 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor'.

questions_answered.question: Do you handle the legal side: documents, witnesses, registry?
questions_answered.evidence: The legal steps themselves are fully explained with official sources and 'Witnesses are optional', and the advisor 'walks you through the exact route to marry legally for your nationality'. It never says they prepare or lodge the documents, so it's guidance rather than 'we handle it'.

questions_answered.question: What is the minimum spend?
questions_answered.evidence: Costs tab and FAQ 4 give no figures; the venue box admits 'fees may be charged either way, with a minimum' but never says what. The registry fee is just 'for a fee'.

questions_answered.question: Can we have a religious ceremony (for example Catholic) here?
questions_answered.evidence: 'A Catholic marriage is legally recognised on its own' (settings and FAQ 3), 'Catholic' in the ceremony type field and in the weekend list.

objections_triggered.objection: Minimum guest numbers or spend that don't fit a small group
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'fees may be charged either way, with a minimum' and 'exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill', with no figure anywhere and 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor' on every region
Largely calmed by the numbered 'Marrying legally, by passport' steps and official links; it's long on a phone and the US/UK blocks add noise, but the Australian part is clear
Palaces, Throne Room, 'a three-day weekend', 'late party', and the only cost band talk is never shown for small groups

trust_signals_noticed: Elopement and 'Under 30' as choices in the qualifier and the form
'Elopements and small weddings are welcome.' in the form intro
Clear numbered legal steps with government sources and 'Checked October 2026'
Nearest airport named for each region
One Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend
turn_offs_noticed: Minimums hidden until the call: 'with a minimum' mentioned but never stated, and the Costs tab has no figure
Much of the imagery and wording is big-scale: palaces, Throne Room, three-day weekend, late party

emotional_response.overall: Relieved on the paperwork, a bit deflated on money
emotional_response.high_point: FAQ 9 and 'Witnesses are optional': it actually pictured the two of us marrying with just family
emotional_response.low_point: Costs tab saying 'depends on five things' with no number

payload.decision_reason: Small groups are clearly welcome (Under 30, Elopement, 'Elopements and small weddings are welcome') and the legal steps are laid out properly with official sources and an advisor to walk us through them, which is my bar. I'll enquire, but only because the form is quick and I can put budget in the notes: the missing minimum spend is the thing that nearly made me save it and keep looking.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Ok, this is the first Portugal page that actually says elopements are welcome and lets me tick 'Under 30'. The legal bit is great, I finally get what documents we need and that we don't even need witnesses. But why does it say there's 'a minimum' and then not tell me what it is? And 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor' on every region, I was looking for that. I'll fill in the form and ask straight out what the minimum is for about 20 of us. If the answer is a 100-guest number, I'm gone.
